title: The Dinosaurs by Jacob Perkins at Playwrights Horizons #playwrightsho...
transcript: Sometimes it's the most ordinary and nondescript places where the most meaningful experiences occur. In The Dinosaurs, a charmingly understated play by Jacob Perkins, that location is a multipurpose room where we see a group of women holding their weekly recovery meeting, sharing their stories, and leaning on their community. This play is both a snapshot and a vast expanse, simultaneously depicting one meeting and an amalgamation of many meetings. You could argue that the play captures an hour of time, or decades — both seem correct. There's a deliberate blurriness here, one that indicates the cyclical nature of time and communities, and the energy of the production is almost meditative. The stories we hear are pretty interesting, but they're mostly self-contained, functioning as individual brush strokes to the bigger picture. This, combined with how the play doesn't establish a clear framework for how it handles time, somewhat muddies its ability to leave a strong emotional impression. That said, it's still in early previews and is already well-developed thematically without being prescriptive. It's the kind of piece that invites projection, enabling different people to take away different things from it and apply their own interpretations. I have plenty of thoughts, but I'm mostly looking forward to hearing what others think. With that, another program for my collection.
